messages.author: efed21dcf7db63c4
messages.subject: EN and RN discrepancy
parts:
Hello,

We are conducting a spatial mark resight analysis via camera traps for a large carnivore. Our goal is to compare camera trapping abundance estimates to the current method that is used to obtain abundance. As such, we are interested in obtaining a reliable estimate of N from our SMR models. We compared AIC between 4 models and our null model was the most supported, with the following region.N() estimate.

fit0 <- secr.fit(CH, mask = HabitatMaskBuffer, trace = FALSE, details = list(knownmarks = FALSE))

null.model <- secr.fit(CH, detectfn = 'HN', model = list(D = ~1, g0= ~1, sigma = ~1), mask =  HabitatMaskBuffer  , trace = FALSE, start = fit0, details = list(knownmarks = FALSE, nsim = 10000)) 

region.N(null.model) 
           estimate     SE.estimate        lcl                    ucl              n
E.N     94.07610     10.654746     75.40186     117.37525     37
R.N     68.88342     4.409934       61.34383     78.75812       37

We are concerned because of the large difference between EN and RN. We reviewed previous posts on this group such as this and this but have additional questions. Specifically, because the above results are from our null model, where density is flat (D ~ 1) and g0 ~ 1, we are stumped why our EN and RN estimates differ. Is this a possible limitation of SMR? We are seeking advice on the potential cause and solutions to move forward.

Thank you for your insight.

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: EN and RN discrepancy
parts: Yes, there is a persistent discrepancy in region.N for all-sighting data with knownmarks = FALSE. RN is defined as the sum of the actual number detected (n) and the expected number that the model says would not be detected, given the estimated total density. Unfortunately (by my oversight) the second component (expected number not detected) is calculated in region.N by applying the wrong 'probability of being missed'. It uses the probability of being missed _conditional on being individually identifiable_ (marked). The calculation should use the unconditional probability of being missed (i.e. allowing for the proportion of animals that were unmarked and intrinsically unidentifiable). We don't estimate the proportion marked as such, and the best estimate is exactly RN = EN. I'm not so sure about the SE, but it's probably closer to 10.65 than 4.4.
